response.content:
### Libraries

Listed below are libraries in Allegheny County. For state-wide library facilities, see [Pennsylvania Archives and Libraries](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Archives_and_Libraries "Pennsylvania Archives and Libraries").

**Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh**  
Pennsylvania Department, Records Research  
4400 Forbes Ave  
Pittsburgh, PA 15213  
Phone: 412-622-3114  
Email: [info@carnegielibrary.org](mailto:info@carnegielibrary.org)  
[Website](http://www.carnegielibrary.org/)  
[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/CarnegieLibraryOfPittsburgh)

* [Genealogy Resources](http://www.carnegielibrary.org/research-overview/genealogy/)
* Birth Registers, City of Pittsburgh (1870-1905); Allegheny City (1885-October, 1907); Allegheny County (1893-1905); McKeesport (1892-1905); Sewickley (1896-1905); Wilkinsburg (1899-1905)
* County Death Registers, City of Pittsburgh (1870-1905); [Online Index for City of Pittsburgh Only](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1810412); Allegheny City (1875-May, 1907); Allegheny County (1893-1905); McKeesport (1887-1905); Sewickley (1894-1905)
* Registers are written entries, not certificates. Birth and Death Certificates are state-issued and are not available for dates prior to 1906.
* After 1906 birth and death certificates are available from the Pennsylvania Department of Health, Division of Vital Records in New Castle, PA.
* [Additional Pittsburgh locations](http://www.carnegielibrary.org/locations/)

**Historic Pittsburgh Digital Library**  
[Website](http://digital.library.pitt.edu/pittsburgh/)  
  
**Pelletier Library**  
Allegheny College  
555 N Main St  
Meadville, PA 16335  
Phone: 814-332-4312  
Email: [library.services@allegheny.edu](mailto:library.services@allegheny.edu)  
[Website](https://sites.allegheny.edu/library/)  
[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/pelletierlibrary/)

### Museums

**Senator John Heinz History Center**   
1212 Smallman St  
Pittsburgh, PA 15222  
Phone: 412-454-6000  
Email: [info@heinzhistorycenter.org](mailto:info@heinzhistorycenter.org)  
[Website](https://www.heinzhistorycenter.org/research/)  
[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/SenatorJohnHeinzHistoryCenter)

* Collection includes 3,500 individual archival collections of families and businesses; over 40,000 books, pamphlets, and monographs, plus 500 maps and atlases.

**Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Hall and Museum**  
4141 Fifth Ave  
Pittsburgh, PA 15213  
Phone: 412-621-4253  
Fax: 412-683-9339  
Email: [info@soldiersandsailorshall.org](mailto:info@soldiersandsailorshall.org)  
[Website](http://soldiersandsailorshall.org/)  
[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/SoldiersandSailors)

* Originally built to honor veterans of the Civil War, but was later expanded to honor soldiers of all conflicts. It contains artifact, interpretive displays, letters, journals, and more.

## Societies

Listed below are societies in Allegheny County. For state-wide genealogical societies, see [Pennsylvania Societies](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Societies "Pennsylvania Societies").

**Afro-American Historical Genealogical Society, Pittsburgh Chapter**   
Pittsburgh, PA  
Email: [pittsburgh@aahgs.org](mailto:pittsburgh@aahgs.org)  
[Website](https://www.aahgs.org/index.cfm?fuseaction=Page.ViewPage&pageId=706)  
[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/aahgs.pgh)  
[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/aahgs/)  
  
**Directory of Pennsylvania Genealogical and Historical Societies**  
[Website](http://www.pennsylvaniaresearch.com/directory-pennsylvania-genealogical-societies.html)  
  
**Historical Society of Pennsylvania**  
1300 Locust St  
Philadelphia, PA 19107  
Phone: 215-732-6200   
Fax: 215-732-2680  
Email: [enews@hsp.org](mailto:enews@hsp.org)  
[Website](http://www.hsp.org/)  
[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/historicalpa/)

[Tips for Planning a Visit.](http://hsp.org/plan-your-visit)

The Genealogical Society of Pennsylvania collects genealogical materials from Pennsylvania and every other state east of the Mississippi River. Its collections also cover pre-migration from Europe, the genealogical “stepping stones” across the Caribbean, and out-migration to Canada. Its collection includes 600,000 printed items and more than 21 million manuscript and graphic items. It is one of the largest family history libraries in the nation, has preeminent printed collections on Pennsylvania and regional history, and offers superb manuscript collections renowned for their strength in 17th-, 18th-, and 19th-century history. By acquiring the holdings of The Balch Institute for Ethnic Studies in 2002 and those of The Genealogical Society of Pennsylvania in 2006, the Society has become a chief center for the documentation and study of the ethnic communities and immigrant experiences between the late 19th century century and our own times.

This table contains the dates the local or state government began recording in the county or county equivalent. Use substitute records for earlier dates. If you believe there is an error, email us at wikisupport@familysearch.org.

County boundary maps are currently unavailable. [Download information instead.](https://publications.newberry.org/ahcb/downloads/states.html)

This website requires a paid subscription for full access. Some subscription websites are available for free at your local [FamilySearch Center or Affiliate Library](https://www.familysearch.org/centers/locations/).

Tombstone transcriptions help when headstones no longer exist. See [The Value of Cemetery Records in Print](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/The_Value_of_Cemetery_Records_in_Print "The Value of Cemetery Records in Print").

Users should [verify](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Verifying_FamilySearch_Historical_Records_Collections_Coverage "Verifying FamilySearch Historical Records Collections Coverage") which locations and dates are included in this collection.

“Current” indicates records are available as recently as privacy laws allow. This date can change from year to year. To determine the exact dates available, contact the respective organization/repository.

FamilySearch affiliate libraries *may* have access to center-only databases, but do not always have all services normally provided by a FamilySearch center.
